posts.text:
“The ceasefire is holding and ceasefire timeline is 21st April – so there are days available,” says retired Pakistani General Muhammad Saeed. Now Pakistan’s field marshal is in Tehran and “I’m very confident that he has some message from the White House… We have great hopes.”

Video

“Nothing about me has changed,” former Congresswoman Marjorie Taylor Greene @FmrRepMTG tells me, having shifted from a true Trump loyalist to a vocal critic. She argues it’s the president who’s changed: “I don’t support the man he’s becoming.”

Video

“President Trump owes Christians an apology,” says his former close ally Marjorie Taylor Greene @FmrRepMTG, calling Trump’s now-deleted AI image of himself as Jesus “blasphemy.”

Video

“Shocked & horrified.” Fmr. Trump ally & congresswoman @FmrRepMTG tells me the president’s Iran rhetoric “gave me grave concern for his mental capacity,” arguing he’s breaking “campaign promises in 2024 to the American people: no more foreign wars, no more foreign regime change.”

Video

“It took me back to my graduate studies and to the Investiture Crisis in the early Middle Ages - a time when rulers took on popes for power and authority.” — @peterfrankopan on the President vs the Pope: substack.com/@peterfrankopan…

“We are in a narrative crisis in America. There are people who want to ignore the harms of our history,” says lawyer and activist Bryan Stevenson. Still, he has hope: “I’m actually feeling more energized, more determined, more committed,” he tells me.

Video

“We’ve never really created cultural institutions in this country that deal honestly with the harms and legacy of slavery,” says Bryan Stevenson of @eji_org. Their new site at Montgomery Square “invite[s] people to have a deeper appreciation of what happened here in Montgomery between 1955 & 1965, a decade that we believe changed the world.”

Video

So great that my special Sarajevo  🎥 teammate gets this overdue recognition:

nytimes.com/2026/04/11/obitu… via @NYTimes

After an extraordinary journey around the moon, the crew of Artemis II have landed back on Earth. Here’s what the late Apollo 11 astronaut Michael Collins told me back in 2019 about the out-of-this-world views you can only see from space.

Video

Despite some relief, Cuba’s humanitarian crisis continues after a US fuel blockade. Under embargo for more than 60 years, I saw up close how Cubans have been struggling for generations in this piece from my archives.

Video

"The death penalty law adopts very clearly a racial approach to the fundamental right to life." In the wake of the passing of the controversial new Israeli death penalty law, I spoke with human rights activists Yuli Novak of B'Tselem and Suhad Bishara of Adalah about what it will mean in practice.

Video

"It's the same people... still in their positions, still ruling over that country in a very repressive way," says @jrezaian. "We might end up making some kind of arrangement with this regime, as we've seen from this wobbly ceasefire. And if we did... that would be essentially the biggest betrayal of the Iranian people."

Video

"One of the ways that Iranians have been asking for help is to be brought back online. You can't organize if you can't communicate with one another. For over 40 days, there's been a near-total blackout of the internet in that country." @jrezaian says, "this time around, as we drop bombs on them, we haven't even been able been able to get them up and running on the internet."

Video

Prominent Iranian human rights lawyer Nasrin Sotoudeh was arrested last week while alone at her home in Tehran. Her family fear for her health and safety and they do not know where she's being held. Nasrin's daughter Mehraveh Khandan sent us this exclusive message.

Video

“The anger is widely spread” in Lebanon, says @DMiliband. “There's anger at Hezbollah for dragging Lebanon into the war. There's anger at Israel for the way in which it's conducting the campaign. There's anger at America. There's anger at their own government. There's a lot of anger, and the tension is high because a whole society is at risk.”

In addition, he says, massive humanitarian aid cuts “are compounding the problem,” with research pointing to an increase in global conflicts since they c

“The great fear in Beirut last week when I was there was that Lebanon would be left out of a deal to end the war in Iran. And the tragedy is that it looks like that fear is now being borne out,” says @RESCUEorg CEO @DMiliband. “I got a text just earlier saying this is the bloodiest day in Beirut for years.”

Video

“There are a lot of voices within Iran today, particularly in the security services, that are talking about returning to the original principles of the revolution, self-reliance and self-dependence, and that leads only to one direction: an autonomous nuclear capability,” warns Ray Takeyh.

“One thing that the Iranian regime recognizes coming out of this war and the last one: if they had the bomb, they wouldn't keep getting bombed.”

Video
